clue.text: Take exercise? Stupid person!

parts.note: to do a subject is to take it as a course of study
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A coach barks an order to get moving, then insults the slacker.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first two words as 'do PE', taking exercise in school terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is slang for a fool or idiot, someone dim-witted.

clue.text: Area served by detective of severe character

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector in the British police
strict means severe or stern

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood policed by a stern detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is a region or area, such as a part of a town.

clue.text: Persistently promote stopper for sink

definitions.meaning: to ... a product is to keep publicising it
the bung that blocks a sink's drain hole

explanation.surface: An advertiser pushing a new sink bung.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: repeated publicity, and the rubber bung closing a drain.

clue.text: First-class relish for food

definitions.meaning: a sauce or garnish put on top of a dish

explanation.surface: Praise for an excellent condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: old British slang for splendid, and a garnish laid over a dish.

clue.text: Sought and found church involved in jazz

indicators.note: being involved in something means sitting within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone searched for and located a church that features in jazz music.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAD jazz is the revivalist New Orleans style popular in 1950s Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace something is to track it down after a search.

clue.text: Satellite state working to create port

indicators.note: working here means being worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A client nation labouring to build a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependent territory controlled and defended by a stronger power is a satellite.

clue.text: Start developing it in a tie

indicators.note: something developing is changing form, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A sports match that begins to unfold while the scores are level.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate is to begin or set something going.

clue.text: Old lady managed to follow golf

indicators.note: the word for managed comes after the golf letter

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to run something is to manage it

explanation.surface: An elderly woman managed to go golfing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gran is a familiar word for grandmother, an elderly woman in the family.

clue.text: Talk too loudly, as bookies might?

definitions.text: Talk too loudly, as bookies might?

parts.words: Talk too loudly, as bookies might?
parts.note: an idiom for speaking boisterously, pictured literally as racecourse bookmakers calling out prices

explanation.surface: A bookmaker bellowing prices at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Bookies are bookmakers, who call out betting prices at race meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to talk loudly and opinionatedly, as if bawling betting prices.

clue.text: Alto in a chorus touring US state

indicators.note: touring means moving around, so these letters are moved about

explanation.surface: An alto singer in a choir on an American tour.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the southeastern states of America, capital Columbia.

clue.text: Service Europeans primarily associated with America

parts.note: US is the United States

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so take only the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Europeans helping out alongside the Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: Service and use both mean benefit or employment, as in 'of service'.

clue.text: Contribution from trendy place?

parts.note: in means fashionable
to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a fashionable venue made a donation.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is what someone contributes to a project, such as ideas or effort.

clue.text: Put down thirteen cards, in informal garment

parts.note: in card games to play a card is to put it down
each suit in a pack has thirteen cards

explanation.surface: A card player laying down a whole suit while casually dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A playsuit is a one-piece casual outfit, typically shorts and top joined.

clue.text: Hold forth, initially dismissing extravagant allegation

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: a claim is an assertion or allegation

explanation.surface: A speaker orating while brushing aside a wild accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to speak rhetorically and at length, as an orator does.

clue.text: Title of chap receiving Northern Ireland politician

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the province's letters go inside

parts.note: Mister is the title used for a man
NI is Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A man's courtesy title is extended to a Belfast politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a government member in charge of a department.

clue.text: Ornate thread's wilfully destroyed

indicators.note: ornate means elaborately worked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone vandalised a fancy embroidery thread.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s belongs to the fodder, supplying the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashed means wrecked or vandalised on purpose.

clue.text: Scoundrel on the up owns country houses

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: A rogue whose fortunes are rising possesses rural properties.
explanation.definitionFit: Dachas are Russian country villas or second homes.

clue.text: Round container mate finally dropped in sea

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: one letter is dropped inside the tin

parts.note: a can is a metal container

indicators.note: finally means taking only the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sailor's round tin is lost overboard as a shipmate finally drops it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is one of the great bodies of salt water, a sea in loose usage.

clue.text: Scottish port's atmosphere, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak means as it is said, so the word for atmosphere is taken by its sound

parts.note: air is the atmosphere around us

explanation.surface: Remarks on the feel of a harbour town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayr is a town on the Firth of Clyde in southwest Scotland; the apostrophe-s stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a harbour town on Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Killer whale in major catastrophe

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A dangerous whale involved in a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is the killer whale, a large black-and-white dolphin.

clue.text: Source of wealth belonging to this compiler

definitions.meaning: a pit yielding gold or coal, or figuratively a rich supply
the setter speaking of something as their own, the first-person possessive

explanation.surface: The setter boasting of their own fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a pit dug for ore, and the possessive pronoun for 'me'.

clue.text: Crazy about a 1960s dance?

parts.note: round can mean about, as in 'round the house'
the Twist was the dance craze of the early 1960s

explanation.surface: Wild enthusiasm for a swinging-sixties dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang idiom for mad or deranged.

clue.text: Painters in dire straits

indicators.note: dire means terrible or in a bad way, so these letters are messed up

explanation.surface: Struggling painters, as the stereotype of the starving artist has it.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters are one example of artists, people who make visual works.

clue.text: Put up with Paddington, for example

definitions.meaning: Paddington is the marmalade-loving ... of children's books

explanation.surface: Tolerating the famous children's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to endure, and the animal Paddington is.
